title: Ln3Q9 as a Molecular Framework for Ion-Size-Driven Assembly of Heterolanthanide (Nd, Er, Yb) Multiple Near-Infrared Emitters

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.formula: NdErYbQ9 (Q = 8-quinolinolato); crystal form C81H54ErN9NdO9Yb·2(CH3CN); bulk analysis consistent with NdErYbQ9·3H2O

material_class.structural_family: trinuclear homoleptic Ln3Q9 8-quinolinolato cluster (central NO7 site; terminal N4O4 sites)

synthesis.procedure: Few drops of 28% aqueous NH3 were added to 8-hydroxyquinoline (0.145 g, 1 mmol) in H2O (100 mL) to a final NH3 concentration of 2.0×10^-2 mol dm^-3 (pH ~10). After 30 min, an aqueous solution of NdCl3·6H2O (0.11 mmol), YbCl3·6H2O (0.11 mmol) and ErCl3·6H2O (0.11 mmol) in water (15 mL) was added. The mixture was refluxed for 2 days until unreacted white ligand disappeared. A yellow precipitate formed, was collected by filtration, washed with water, 0.1 M NaOH and water, and dried in an oven at 60 °C (yield >95%). Yellow crystals for X-ray diffraction were obtained by recrystallization from CH3CN.
synthesis.time: 30 min ligand deprotonation, then reflux 2 days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous reflux; filtration; oven drying; recrystallization from acetonitrile
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow precipitate filtered, washed with water, 0.1 M NaOH and water, dried at 60 °C; yellow crystals from CH3CN.

properties.summary: Discrete Nd/Er/Yb quinolinolato trimer is a multiple NIR emitter: ligand excitation produces residual green ligand fluorescence (~520 nm) plus simultaneous Nd, Yb and Er NIR bands covering ~900–1650 nm in DMSO. Efficient Yb→Er energy transfer is inferred from equally intense Er emission versus the Er/Yb analogue. Crystal-field splitting broadens f–f bands according to site occupancy.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.formula: ErxYb3−xQ9, best described as ErYb2Q9 (Q = 8-quinolinolato); crystal form C81H54ErN9O9Yb2·2(CH3CN); bulk analysis consistent with ErYb2Q9·3H2O

material_class.structural_family: trinuclear homoleptic Ln3Q9 8-quinolinolato cluster (Er/Yb nearly vicariant on terminal vs central sites)

synthesis.procedure: Prepared analogously to 1: to a water solution (100 mL) containing 1 mmol of 8-hydroxyquinoline (deprotonated as in 1 with aqueous NH3), a mixture of YbCl3·6H2O (0.22 mmol) and Er(CH3COO)3·6H2O (0.11 mmol) in water (15 mL) was added. A yellow precipitate formed, was collected by filtration, washed with water, 0.1 M NaOH and water, and dried in an oven at 60 °C (yield >95%). Yellow crystals suitable for X-ray studies were obtained by recrystallization from CH3CN.
synthesis.time: same procedure as 1 (reflux until ligand consumed)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous reflux analogous to 1; filtration; oven drying; recrystallization from acetonitrile
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow precipitate filtered, washed with water, 0.1 M NaOH and water, dried at 60 °C; yellow crystals from CH3CN.

properties.summary: Heterobimetallic Er/Yb Ln3Q9 shows simultaneous Yb (~1 μm) and Er (~1.5 μm) NIR photoluminescence after ligand excitation, plus residual ligand fluorescence at ~520 nm. Er band intensity matches that of trimetallic 1, supporting efficient Yb–Er energy transfer. Band shapes differ slightly from 1, consistent with different Er/Yb site occupancies.
